question: What lay unrecognised beneath the swamp forests of the central Congo Basin until 2017?
answer: The largest tropical peatland known. Coring the swamps by hand, Dargie and colleagues mapped about 145,000 km² of peat, larger than England, holding roughly 30 billion tonnes of carbon: about three years of the world's fossil-fuel emissions. Permanent waterlogging stops dead leaves rotting, so they pile up for millennia under the trees.
move: The biggest store in a system can be the one nobody thought to dig for.
reference: Dargie et al., Age, extent and carbon storage of the central Congo Basin peatland complex, Nature, 2017
